summary:
Prover, about 90 minutes. Pencil first, then numpy on the orchestrator's own rule code; five pictures made and looked at. No Mandelbrot solid drawn or looked at; nothing registered with the bench. Long notes: out/r20/prover/NOTES.md.

W1, W3, W4 hold exactly. W2 holds with a better reason. W5 is half wrong and half proved. W6 is half right and half wrong.

- W1 HOLDS: one step sends the planes at 60 and 120 degrees into the flat plane (|Z| <= 3e-14) and the cuts equal the flat set at 0 of 160,801 points for basilica, rabbit, Siegel (dendrite: 1 point, rounding). Amendment: the 60-degree copy is the MIRROR image (the three copies are the flat picture turned 0, 120, 240 degrees).
- W2 HOLDS, reason sharpened: with even k the cut z = 0 is still right for c on the x-axis (0 points differ) and wrong off it (rabbit 88.9 % of points, Siegel 100 %). Clean statement (parity): a fold-free rule exact on the flat plane has an EVEN number of extra half-planes on each side of it, at every power. One a side (two planes) is exactly what cannot be had.
- W3 HOLDS (5.5e-14); six-fold for c on the x-axis.
- W4 HOLDS on all four counts (0.0000 % reversed, covers 5.994 times, six crushed directions, six bud directions with stretch 2.0000 x 2.0000, +x reached only from +-x). Left out: the x-axis is a line of cone points, stretch 2 x 2 up to 2 x 10 right beside it.
- W5 first half FAILS for the sinus profile: buds in the planes are ovals 0.98, 1.29, 1.32, 1.48 long-to-thin at generations 1 to 4 (one-plane twins 0.86, 0.99, 0.95); an exact 10-degree band brings them to 0.86, 1.09, 1.05, 1.12. Second half HOLDS and is proved for every member: only 33 %, 11 %, 3.7 % of buds at generations 2, 3, 4 lie in the planes; the rest are fins, median 5.5, 6.9, 14.6 to 1 (largest 126 to 1), median thickness 0.014, 0.0048, 0.0013. At every neck the skin between the planes is a comb of hair-thin slivers (seen).
- W6 first half HOLDS to two figures: Siegel half-thickness 0.0097, 0.0045, 0.0022, 0.0011 at 60, 240, 960, 3840 steps against pencil 0.0090, 0.0045, 0.0022, 0.0011: a sheet. Second half FAILS: an exact band gives a body that keeps its thickness, but only 0.062 (band 10) or 0.126 (band 20) against the one-plane rule's 0.468: a wedge with flat faces meeting on the x-axis.
- C1 forbids a second plane that the rule KEEPS; the copy planes are not kept (one step into the flat plane, never back), so the rule is outside C1.
- Two planes with an exact flat cut: three ways tried, all fail (even winding, lopsided winding, one fold).
- Right k: odd is forced; the roundness count asks for k = n; so k = n at odd powers and n + 1 at even powers (the entry's formula). At power 2 the count the power asks for (k = 2, the two-plane look) is the forbidden case.
- A ten-second scout of the same rule wound round the y-axis FAILS (frayed flake, streaked neck).

verdicts.name: W1
verdicts.what: For every c in the flat plane the cut by the plane at 60 and at 120 degrees is the flat picture, turned.
verdicts.verdict: holds (exactly), with one amendment: the copy at 60 degrees is the mirror image; as planes the copies are the flat picture turned 0, 120 and 240 degrees
verdicts.evidence: Reasoned: a point of the half-plane at j x 60 degrees is sent by T to the flat plane, half y > 0 for even j and y < 0 for odd j; from then on it is a flat orbit; nothing uses the slope of g or which c. Measured (logs/exact.log, logs/extra.log): |Z| <= 3e-14 after one step; error 7e-15 against (x + i rho)^2 at 0, 120, 240 degrees and against (x - i rho)^2 at 60, 180, 300; whole cuts at 60 steps differ from the (mirrored) flat set at 0 of 160,801 points for basilica, rabbit, Siegel, 1 point for the dendrite. Seen: two-planes.png bottom right.
verdicts.gates: exact.py block W1 + escape-step check: all pass

verdicts.name: W2
verdicts.what: k must be odd: an even k breaks the cut z = 0.
verdicts.verdict: holds, but the stated reason is loose: with even k the cut z = 0 is still the flat set for c on the x-axis; it is wrong for c off it. Clean form: parity rule
verdicts.evidence: Measured: k = 2 and 4 give conj(z^2) on the half y < 0 (error 0 against it, 37 against z^2); basilica cut z = 0 differs at 0 of 19,541 points; rabbit at 88.9 % of its points; Siegel 100 % (cut empty). Seen: two-planes.png top middle (a rabbit folded on the x-axis). Reasoned (parity): exactness forces g(0) = 0, g(180) = 180 + whole turns; a rising g then puts 2m (even) extra half-planes strictly above the flat plane; with the mirror above/below k = 2m + 1 is odd. Holds at every power.
verdicts.gates: exact.py block W2: as expected

verdicts.name: W3
verdicts.what: F is unchanged by a 120-degree turn about the x-axis, so every Julia set has that symmetry for every c.
verdicts.verdict: holds (exactly)
verdicts.evidence: Measured 5.5e-14 on 200,000 points; control F(turn 60) - F = 50. Also measured to 6e-14: F(turn 60) = half turn of F (six-fold symmetry for c on the x-axis), both mirrors, the half turn about the upright axis, F(-v) = mirror of F(v). One sentence on the other solid: it keeps the two mirrors only, not the three-fold turn (reasoned; not drawn).
verdicts.gates: exact.py block W3: pass

verdicts.name: W4
verdicts.what: Folds nothing; crushes only the six directions half way between the planes at right angles to the x-axis (sent straight up or down); the six bud directions arrive with stretch exactly 2; only +x and -x go to +x.
verdicts.verdict: holds on all four counts; leaves out that the whole x-axis is a line of cone points
verdicts.evidence: Measured on 600,000 directions: 0.0000 % mirror-reversed, covers 5.994 times, area factor < 0.02 only within 0.7 degrees of the half-way turns and 3.6 degrees of the plane x = 0; the six bud directions sent to (-1, 0, 0) with stretches 2.0000 and 2.0000; of 3,000,000 directions 100 land within 1 degree of +x, all by +x or -x. Left out: 0.5 degree from +x the stretches are 2 x 2 in a copy plane, 2 x 4 at 10 degrees, 2 x 8 at 20, 2 x 10 half way. Squeeze round the axis / along the meridian equals g'(a) to 5e-8 everywhere.
verdicts.gates: exact.py block W4: pass

verdicts.name: W5, first half
verdicts.what: A bud whose centre lies in one of the three planes is as round as its flat twin, at every depth.
verdicts.verdict: broken for the sinus profile: ovals that get slowly thinner with depth; true to about 10 % with an exact band
verdicts.evidence: Measured (logs/fins-sin3.log, fins-one.log, fins-band10.log), width along the meridian / round the axis at generations 1 to 4: m_w3 0.98, 1.29, 1.32 (1.19 to 1.45), 1.48 (1.31 to 1.76); one-plane twins 0.86, 0.99, 0.95; exact band 10 degrees 0.86, 1.09, 1.05, 1.12. Reasoned: g' = 1 only ON the plane; across a bud 5 degrees wide it reaches 1.27 and the squeeze adds up over the ancestors. Seen: fins-unrolled.png top row (ovals on the green lines for m_w3, rounder for the band).
verdicts.gates: 6, 12, 24, 48 buds measured point by point at 80 steps

verdicts.name: W5, second half
verdicts.what: A bud between the planes is squeezed thin round the x-axis by the slope of g, and its own buds by more, without limit; fins cannot be removed in this kind.
verdicts.verdict: holds, and proved for every member of the kind (any g going k >= 2 times round)
verdicts.evidence: Measured: generation 2 has 24 fins at x = +-1.041, turned 23.6 and 36.4 degrees (pencil the same), 0.076 long, 0.065 tall, 0.014 thick, 5.5 to 1 (pencil g' = 4.57 times the 1.2 above). Generation 3: 192 of 216 buds between the planes, median 6.9 to 1, largest 28, 12 % thinner than 20 to 1. Generation 4: 1248 of 1296, median 14.6 to 1, largest 126, 40 % thinner than 20 to 1, median thickness 0.0013. Even winding: every bud a sliver (2.6, 9, 24, 37 to 1). Seen: fins-unrolled.png (slivers under the predicted ticks), neck-unrolled.png (a comb between the planes at 0.118, 0.048, 0.018 from the neck; clean only within about 5 degrees of the copy planes). Proof (reasoned): near a neck on the x-axis the rule is (x, rho, a) -> (x^2, 2|x| rho, g(a)), measured to 6 figures; so the k^m copies of one bud, m steps deeper, lie on ONE circle round the axis with equal length and height; only 360/D of them fit at full width; the average is thinner by k^m D / 360.
verdicts.gates: fins.py on sin3, lin3, band10, one-plane; near-axis form checked in logs/extra.log

verdicts.name: W6, first half
verdicts.what: Where g(a) is further from the flat plane than a, a body that neither attracts nor repels across the flat plane (Siegel disc) collapses to a sheet.
verdicts.verdict: holds, to two figures against pencil
verdicts.evidence: Pencil: at the disc's middle h -> h (1 + 103 h^2) for m_w3, so a height stays N steps only below 1/sqrt(206 N). Measured half-thickness 0.0147, 0.0097, 0.0064, 0.0045, 0.0031, 0.0022, 0.0015, 0.0011 at 30 to 3840 steps; pencil 0.0127, 0.0090, 0.0064, 0.0045, 0.0032, 0.0022, 0.0016, 0.0011. One-plane rule 0.468 at every count. m_w5 thinner still (0.0040 at 60 steps); m_w3lin below 0.0002 at every count; m_w3f a wafer thinning slowly to 0.013. Seen: siegel-thickness.png (three thin lines at 0 and +-60 degrees, thinner at 480 steps than at 60).
verdicts.gates: siegel.py, 7 rules x 3 spots x 8 step counts

verdicts.name: W6, second half
verdicts.what: A profile with g(a) = a exactly in a band round the flat plane would give the Siegel disc the one-plane rule's thickness.
verdicts.verdict: broken as worded: it gives a body that does not thin, but a wedge, 13 % (band 10) or 27 % (band 20) as thick as the one-plane body
verdicts.evidence: Measured half-thickness at the middle: band 10 degrees 0.0615, band 20 degrees 0.1258, the same at every step count from 30 to 3840; pencil |y| tan(w) = 0.0596 and 0.1229; one-plane 0.468. Toward the x-axis less: band 10 gives 0.038 and 0.015 at 30 % and 60 % of the way to the point 0. Seen: siegel-thickness.png right column: a six-sided wedge with two flat faces meeting in a point on the x-axis, ragged loose specks at its far end.
verdicts.gates: siegel.py

verdicts.name: C1 and this rule
verdicts.what: What exactly C1 forbids and why wind-then-square is not forbidden.
verdicts.verdict: holds: C1 forbids a second plane or smooth sheet that the rule KEEPS for c off the x-axis; the copy planes are not kept
verdicts.evidence: Reasoned from the round-17 proof (hypothesis: the plane is mapped into itself, so the crossing line is kept by z^2 + c). Here one step sends the planes at 60 and 120 degrees into the flat plane (measured |Z| <= 3e-14) and they never return; the crossing line is treated like every other line of the plane, so no condition on c arises. Price not named by C1: a plane that is not kept cannot keep its surroundings round after the first step; that is where the fins come from.
verdicts.gates: n/a (argument); one-step measurement in exact.py

verdicts.name: Two planes with an exact flat cut
verdicts.what: Is there any way to have TWO planes (k = 2, or a winding with one fold) and keep the flat cut exact?
verdicts.verdict: no: three ways tried, each fails for a stated reason
verdicts.evidence: (1) Even winding k = 2: flat cut wrong off the x-axis (rabbit 88.9 %). (2) Lopsided k = 2 (once round above, three half turns below): flat exact to 5e-15 and fold-free, but both extra half-planes lie below (240 and 300 degrees, measured), are not one plane, and the mirror above/below is off by 49. (3) One fold a side: flat exact, mirror kept, upright plane sent into the flat plane, but both halves land on y < 0, so its picture is the lower half doubled by a mirror: equal to the flat set for the basilica (0 points), not the rabbit (11,505 points differ; 43 from the doubled half); and it is the closed fold-before-squaring kind. General (reasoned): with the mirror above/below the upright plane can never carry both halves of the flat picture. Seen: two-planes.png.
verdicts.gates: exact.py block TWO planes

verdicts.name: A member whose between-plane bodies do not thin
verdicts.what: Is there one, or a proof that there is none?
verdicts.verdict: there is none (proved by a count, for any g going at least twice round; a staircase g does not escape)
verdicts.evidence: The proof under W5 second half. Measured on three profiles: sinus, even winding, exact band 10 degrees all thin with depth (band 10 between the planes: 5.6, 7.6, 17 to 1 at generations 2, 3, 4).
verdicts.gates: fins.py on three profiles

verdicts.name: The right k for a whole power n
verdicts.what: By a principle, not taste.
verdicts.verdict: k = n when n is odd, n + 1 when n is even (the entry's formula). At power 2 the count the power asks for, k = 2, is forbidden
verdicts.evidence: Principle 1 (parity, reasoned; measured flat error 1e-14 to 1e-11 for odd k at powers 2 to 5, 240 and 1200 for even k): k odd at every power. Principle 2 (the count, measured): covers n k times: 5.99, 8.99, 19.98, 24.97 for (2,3), (3,3), (4,5), (5,5); round on average needs n^2. They agree at odd powers (9 = 3^2, 25 = 5^2); at even powers n + 1 is the smallest allowed count not below what the power asks for (n - 1 at power 2 is the one-plane rule), over-covering by 1.5 at power 2 and 1.25 at power 4.
verdicts.gates: exact.py blocks 'The count' and 'Flat plane exact'

verdicts.name: The count check
verdicts.what: Round bodies on average need the sphere covered n^2 times; P covers it n times and T k times.
verdicts.verdict: holds; it does not rescue the fins
verdicts.evidence: Measured mean area factor = n k for 8 pairs; root-mean-square stretch 2.45 against 2 at power 2 with k = 3, 3.00 against 3 at power 3 with k = 3. The count is right at odd powers, yet the proof of the fins holds for every k >= 2 at every power.
verdicts.gates: exact.py

verdicts.name: Powers 3 and up: a symmetry lost
verdicts.what: The flat picture of z^n has an n-fold turn about the upright axis. Does the solid keep it?
verdicts.verdict: broken at powers 3, 4, 5; kept at power 2
verdicts.evidence: Measured on unit vectors: the one-plane rule changes by 2e-15 under that turn at every power; wind-then-square by 0.00 at power 2 and by a median 1.04, 1.31, 1.23 at powers 3, 4, 5. So at power 3 the flat cut has a three-fold turn that the solid lacks: the x-axis is singled out among three equal axes. Tested on F (one step), not on drawn sets.
verdicts.gates: exact.py block 'Power-n symmetry'

verdicts.name: Scout: wound round the y-axis instead
verdicts.what: The same rule with the winding axis on the bud axis, so that no neck lies on the axis. Ten seconds, not gated, not registered.
verdicts.verdict: fail at first look: frayed flake, streaked neck

recommendation:
The right k for a whole power n is: k = n when n is odd, k = n + 1 when n is even. It rests on two things. First, a parity rule (reasoned, checked at powers 2 to 5): a fold-free rule that is exact on the flat plane and the same above and below must wind an odd number of times, at every power. Second, the count (measured): the rule covers the sphere of directions n k times and round-on-average needs n squared, so the power asks for k = n. At odd powers both agree. At even powers k = n is forbidden, n - 1 under-covers (at power 2 it is the one-plane rule itself) and n + 1 is the smallest allowed count that is not below what the power asks for. So the entry's formula is right and is not a dial.

What cannot be had:
1. Two planes at power 2. The count the power asks for is k = 2, four buds round the axis, the two-plane basilica the user liked. That is exactly the forbidden case: even winding breaks the flat cut off the x-axis, a lopsided winding puts both extra half-planes on one side, one fold gives a mirror-doubled half picture.
2. A count that moves with every power: the count round the x-axis is 2k = 6, 6, 10, 10 for powers 2, 3, 4, 5.
3. Round bodies between the planes: proved impossible for every member of the kind. Fins are the large majority of buds at depth and stand as combs at every neck.
4. A Siegel body with the one-plane thickness: a band gives a wedge at best.
5. At powers 3 and up, the flat picture's own turning symmetry about the upright axis: the solid does not have it.

For the texts of the lab entry: say "turned by a third of a turn" for the copies (the 60-degree one is mirrored), say that the buds in the planes are slightly oval, that between the planes the buds are thin fins that get thinner with depth, and that the Siegel disc is a sheet.

My odds: about 85 % that the rule fails "clean close up" there by panel2's own line, as `along` did, since the comb is forced by a count and no profile removes it. If it does fail, the kind is closed for a clean skin and the only open question is whether the fins are small enough to be accepted by eye; the profile to judge that on is an exact band of about 10 degrees (rounder buds in the planes, a Siegel wedge instead of a sheet, fins no better). recommendation:
ONE form: w_c15. Planes at multiples of 60 degrees; d = angle to the nearest plane; the wound angle is (plane number) x 180 degrees plus or minus h(d), with h(d) = d for d <= 15 degrees and h(d) = 15 + 5 (d - 15) for 15 < d <= 30 degrees. For a general odd k: band 90/(2k) degrees, ramp slope 2k - 1.

Principle, no free size: slope exactly 1 near every plane, and nowhere steeper than the smooth sinus form is at its steepest (2k - 1). The widest bands that allows are half of the way to the mid plane, and the ramp between them is then forced to be straight. This is a convention with a reason (I measured that steepness is what breaks the sets off the planes), not a derivation from the squaring; I found none.

Why this one: it has the same steepest slope and cliff number as m_w3 and beats or equals it on every line I measured: bud at 60 degrees exactly as round as its flat twin (1.05 against 0.93), ribs on the buds 1.24 and 1.19 % against 2.10 and 1.56, Siegel disc 0.091 thick and staying (95 % against 71 %), rabbit thickest 0.323 against 0.260 and biggest piece 95.6 against 82.1 %, nudged basilicas 0.165 and 0.299 thick against 0.148 and 0.160 and not leaking over 1,000 steps. Where it is worse: a visible corner in the outline 15 degrees either side of each plane, ribs on the middle body 0.27 against 0.18 % (line 0.45), and panel2 labels bas_yz 'outside' for it.

By pictures alone the 25 degree band has the cleanest basilica skin, but it loses the nudged basilica completely, so it is out. If the crease shows in the lab, use w_c15r (corner rounded over 3 degrees; numbers as good, one extra size). It does not pass: bench J8 fails, the skin is hairy at every scale, and panel2 fails it on all 10 sets it judges.
best_next: Put w_c15's profile into the lab entry beside the sinus (three lines: nearest plane, band test, straight ramp) and look at the Siegel disc, the rabbit and the basilica close up in the real renderer at 40 steps or more; check that the distance estimate copes with the slope-5 crease, and fall back to w_c15r if the crease shows. Odds: about 4 in 5 that the Siegel disc and rabbit look clearly better than with the sinus (the sinus's Siegel disc is a draining film); about 1 in 2 that the basilica looks any different to a person at normal zoom; practically nil that any profile of this rule passes panel2, because the comb of fins and the three crossing copies are properties of winding k times, not of g. The honest decision for the orchestrator is therefore not which profile, but whether to show the user the kind at all with its faults named.
